footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net income to common: after income tax and $9.9M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) rose 11.7% to $1.1B in 2025. Net interest income rose 9.9% to $909M and noninterest income rose 23.5% to $154M; noninterest expense rose 2.4%, and the provision for credit losses was $48.8M, versus $51.0M.
Net income to common rose 30.1% to $318M, or $2.62 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 55.7% versus 60.7%. United Community Banks returned $163M through dividends and buybacks.
highlights: Net income to common rose 30.1% to $318M.
watch: Net interest income depends on interest rates.
